traditional_knowledge: ”A la hora de sembrar debes considerar la temperatura y el momento en que tendrás agua disponible”. When sowing, you must take into account the temperature and the moment when water will be at your disposal.
underlying_assumption: The timing of seeding is limited by temperature and the availability of water.

traditional_knowledge: ”Según las propiedades del suelo, los cultivos pueden dar resultados distintos, por ejemplo: en terrenos arenosos las sandías adquieren más dulzor, mientras que los melones se ’apepinan’ y quedan sin sabor”. The way crops turn out can vary according to the soil's properties. For instance: in sandy soils watermelons gain sweetness; melons, by contrast, turn ”cucumber-like” and lose their flavor.
underlying_assumption: The characteristics of the soil affect how crops develop.

traditional_knowledge: ”Riego cada 8 días. Cuando alguna planta requiere más agua, la riego cada 4 días”. I do the watering every 8 days. When some plant requires more water, I irrigate it every 4 days.
underlying_assumption: The water needs of crops can be met by reducing the interval between one watering and the next.

traditional_knowledge: ”El limón verna necesita una cantidad de agua inferior a la del liso.” The Verna lemon needs a smaller amount of water than the smooth lemon.
underlying_assumption: Certain fruit tree varieties consume less water than other varieties.

traditional_knowledge: "En el caso de los frutales, no queda otra opción que regar." When it comes to fruit trees, irrigating is unavoidable.
underlying_assumption: Fruit trees require large quantities of water.

traditional_knowledge: ”Si la fulla de l'arbre o les herbes que hi ha al costat no es veuen alegres, cal regar-ne més.” If the leaves of the tree or the nearby weeds don't appear happy, you need to water more.
underlying_assumption: Foliage that looks wilted or dull signals that more irrigation is needed.

traditional_knowledge: ”El perer demana més aigua que no pas el presseguer. El pomer no en requereix tanta.” The pear tree demands more water than the peach tree does. The apple tree does not require as much of it.
underlying_assumption: Water requirements vary among distinct tree species.

traditional_knowledge: ”Quan l'arbre és més jove, menor és la quantitat de reg que necessita.” When a tree is younger, the amount of watering it requires is smaller.
underlying_assumption: The water needs of young trees are lower.

traditional_knowledge: ”Empleo alcorques para dar riego a los árboles”. I employ tree basins to irrigate the trees.
underlying_assumption: Focusing water in the root zone enhances how efficiently irrigation works.

traditional_knowledge: ”Dentro de mi finca reservo espacios que no cultivo con el fin de que broten hierbas silvestres, y varias de ellas resultan útiles, como la caléndula (Calendula) y la malva (Malva sylvestris)”. In my farm I set aside spaces that I don't cultivate so wild herbs can sprout; several of them turn out to be useful, like calendula and mallow.
underlying_assumption: Wild herbs are capable of offering both ecological and practical advantages.

traditional_knowledge: "El aire en movimiento reseca bastante las plantaciones". Moving air considerably dries out the plantations.
underlying_assumption: Wind raises the rate of evapotranspiration.

traditional_knowledge: ”La lluvia del cielo no suprime el riego de las hortalizas, pero en el arbolado sí que puede suprimir algún riego (el árbol no requiere tanta agua).” Water falling from the sky does not remove irrigation for vegetables, though for trees it can remove some irrigation (the tree does not require so much water).
underlying_assumption: Trees need less water than vegetable crops do.

traditional_knowledge: ”Siembro cultivos que tienen las mismas necesidades unos junto a otros”. I sow crops that have the same requirements next to one another.
underlying_assumption: Clustering plants that need comparable amounts of water makes watering more efficient.

traditional_knowledge: ”Hay que dar riego a las patatas cada 10 días mientras crecen”. Potatoes need to be irrigated every ten days while they grow.
underlying_assumption: Consistent watering at set intervals with even spacing satisfies the water requirements of potatoes as they develop.

traditional_knowledge: ”Durante las épocas de más calor, el trigo resiste mayores intervalos entre un riego y otro que las hortalizas”. During the hottest periods, wheat endures greater gaps between one watering and the next than vegetables do.
underlying_assumption: During hot periods, wheat can withstand longer gaps between irrigations than vegetable crops.

traditional_knowledge: ”Cuando riegas de más, debes prestar atención y llevar a cabo el control de hongos.” When you irrigate excessively, you must be careful and carry out fungus control.
underlying_assumption: An excess of water may lead to the emergence of fungus.

traditional_knowledge: "Siembro en el momento en que siembra mi vecino." I sow at the time my neighbor sows.
underlying_assumption: Irrigators follow a sowing schedule that resembles that of the people living next to them.

traditional_knowledge: ”Los cultivos de huerta requieren mayor cantidad de agua.” Vegetable garden crops use up more water.
underlying_assumption: Vegetable garden crops (as opposed to trees) require a greater amount of water.

traditional_knowledge: "Determino la cantidad de agua a aplicar observando el cultivo: el grado de marchitez de la planta, lo arrugadas que están las hojas, y cavo para comprobar si las raíces tienen agua." I determine the amount of water to apply by observing the crop: the degree to which the plant is wilted, how wrinkled the leaves appear, and I dig to check whether the roots have water.
underlying_assumption: Watching and touching the plant and soil conditions yields information useful for making irrigation decisions.

traditional_knowledge: ”Ciertos cultivos necesitan regarse por completo, mientras que otros únicamente hasta la mitad.” Certain crops must be irrigated all the way up, whereas others only need it to the halfway point.
underlying_assumption: The depth to which crops must be irrigated varies from one crop to another.

traditional_knowledge: ”Ponemos maleza encima del cultivo para evitar que el agua se evapore tan deprisa.” We place weeds over the crop to prevent the water from evaporating so fast.
underlying_assumption: Placing a layer of vegetation over crops decreases the loss of water through evaporation.

traditional_knowledge: ”Cuando hay hortalizas regamos anegando solo hasta media altura del caballón.” When there are vegetables, we water by flooding only halfway up the ridge.
underlying_assumption: How deep the irrigation reaches varies according to the kind of crop.

traditional_knowledge: ”Según el tipo de cultivo, lo que varía es cada cuánto se riega, y nada más.” Depending on the type of crop, what varies is how often watering is done, and nothing else.
underlying_assumption: How often irrigation occurs is determined by the crop rather than by a set schedule.

traditional_knowledge: ”En el caso del cilantro y el perejil, el primer riego debe cubrir el cultivo, mientras que el segundo no.” In the case of coriander and parsley, the crop should be covered by the first watering, whereas the second should not.
underlying_assumption: For certain crops, the way they are watered has to be modified according to how developed they are.

traditional_knowledge: ”El cultivo determina la cantidad de agua que aplico (soy yo quien lo decide)”. The type of crop determines how much water I put on it (I am the one who decides).
underlying_assumption: How much water is applied depends on the water needs of each individual crop.

traditional_knowledge: ”Cuando hay sequía, detengo el riego apenas el agua alcanza la cola.” When there is drought, I stop the irrigation the moment the water arrives at the bottom of the plot.
underlying_assumption: During a drought, the duration of irrigation is shortened.

traditional_knowledge: ”Cuanto se planta en luna menguante da mejores frutos”. Whatever is planted while the moon is waning produces better results.
underlying_assumption: Plants seeded when the moon is waning grow and develop more successfully.

traditional_knowledge: "La planta te lo indica (cuando le hace falta agua), y las hierbas del campo también lucen más apagadas". The crop signals it to you (when it lacks water), and the wild herbs of the field likewise appear duller.
underlying_assumption: The requirement for water can be verified by sight both in the crops and in the herbs that are growing.

traditional_knowledge: "Los cultivos que permanecían más tiempo en el bancal eran el trigo, la cebada y la alfalfa. La alfalfa se plantaba en eras y, conforme la cortabas, seguía brotando. Resultaba imprescindible para el ganado". The crops that stayed longest in the plot were wheat, barley and alfalfa. Alfalfa was planted on threshing floors and, as you cut it, it kept sprouting. It was indispensable for livestock.
underlying_assumption: The crops that stay longest in the plot are wheat, barley and alfalfa, alfalfa being notable for its capacity to grow back after being cut several times.

traditional_knowledge: "Las hierbas dañinas le quitan el agua a las plantaciones." Harmful weeds take away water from the plantations.
underlying_assumption: Weeds and crops compete with one another for the available water.

traditional_knowledge: ”Cuando las hojas del limonero aparecen arrugadas, esto señala que el cultivo no está recibiendo suficiente agua.” When lemon tree leaves appear wrinkled, this signals that the crop is not receiving enough water.
underlying_assumption: A shortage of water is signalled by wrinkled tree leaves.

traditional_knowledge: ”Almaceno el agua que reúno de los tejados y con ella riego algunos frutales”. I store the water I gather from the roofs and with it I water some fruit trees.
underlying_assumption: Rooftop-collected and stored water is suitable for irrigation.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Cuando las acequias se encuentran en mal estado, el agua se va desperdiciando". When the ditches are in bad shape, water gets wasted.
underlying_assumption: The loss of water may occur if the irrigation ditches are in a bad state.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "El momento ideal para el riego es al alba o al ocaso, cuando ya no aprieta tanto el calor". The ideal time for irrigation is at daybreak or sunset, when the heat is no longer so intense.
underlying_assumption: Irrigating during the cooler times of day (daybreak/sunset) reduces the amount of water lost through evaporation.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "El propio cultivo te avisa cuando necesita agua y cuando la tiene de más". The crop itself signals to you when it needs water and when it has an excess of it.
underlying_assumption: A shortage or surplus of water can show itself in the plant.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”El agua resulta fría, aunque se vuelve muy caliente cuando te la arrebatan.” Although water is cold, it becomes very hot when someone takes it from you.
underlying_assumption: Stealing water triggers grave disputes.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Si se quiere que la parcela quede cubierta con un dedo de agua al final, al principio debe cubrirse con 4-5 dedos.” If you want the plot covered with one finger of water at the end, at the start it should be covered with 4-5 fingers.
underlying_assumption: The depth of applied water needs to be greater near the channel so that surplus water flows by gravity to the far end of the plot.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "En otros tiempos, los ancianos no malgastaban ni una sola gota de agua." Long ago, the elderly people never let a single drop of water go to waste.
underlying_assumption: Elder irrigators managed water with great efficiency.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”En la huerta se trabaja mediante el intercambio de jornadas: hoy yo te echo una mano y mañana tú me la echas a mí.” In the orchard, people operate through the exchange of workdays: today I lend you a hand, and tomorrow you lend one to me.
underlying_assumption: Reciprocity is the basis on which irrigation depends.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Construyo las eras con menos anchura, de esa manera ahorro más agua". I build the threshing floors with less width, that way I conserve more water.
underlying_assumption: Making the threshing floors less wide enables more efficient use of water.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Es necesario reparar secciones de las galerías y las acequias para impedir que haya filtraciones”. It is necessary to fix parts of the galleries and irrigation channels to stop leaks from occurring.
underlying_assumption: Maintaining and mending the infrastructure keeps water from leaking.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Aquí existen ciertas fuentes desde las que el riego se hace a hilo, mientras que en otras disponen de balsa”. There are certain springs here from which watering is done directly, while at others they possess a pond.
underlying_assumption: Using the springs, irrigation can be carried out directly from their flow or that flow can be kept in ponds.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Cuando el agua es poca, planto una cantidad menor de cultivos". When there is little water, I plant a smaller amount of crops.
underlying_assumption: When water runs short, it is not possible to keep the same extent of land in use.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Igualmente (en época de escasez) elevo el nivel del agua en la acequia, aunque eso requiere más tiempo”. Likewise (during shortages) I bring up the water level in the ditch, though that requires more time.
underlying_assumption: Raising the water level within the ditch by gathering additional flow and partly shutting the outlet assists in enabling irrigation with suitable pressure.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Fui aprendiendo a base de perder el agua una y otra vez". I came to know it through repeatedly letting the water get away from me.
underlying_assumption: Doing flood irrigation efficiently is something that comes with practice.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Cuando dispongo de menos agua, no doy riego a los árboles frutales en todas las tandas”. When I have less water available, I don't irrigate the fruit trees during every shift.
underlying_assumption: During a scarcity of water, certain crops take precedence over others.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "El agua se la disputa la hierba." Weeds are competition for water.
underlying_assumption: Crops must compete against weeds to obtain water.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "El riego por inundación exige que la tierra esté nivelada." Flood irrigation demands that the land be leveled.
underlying_assumption: To carry out flood irrigation correctly, the ground within your plot must be leveled.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Sin malas hierbas: hay menos competencia y menor gasto de agua. Es posible ampliar los intervalos entre riegos.” Free of weeds: there is less competition and lower water use. It is possible to lengthen the intervals between waterings.
underlying_assumption: When crops have no weeds, the entire water use is directed to the plantation.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Si aparece un 'tollo', el agua se escapa por él; es preciso introducir la mano y cerrar el orificio.” If a 'tollo' appears, water escapes through it; you have to insert your hand and close up the opening.
underlying_assumption: To avoid losing water, the plot terraces must be repaired.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Cuando la arbolea no lo necesita, regarla es acabar con ella." When the tree has no need for it, watering it amounts to killing it.
underlying_assumption: Giving the crop excessive water harms its growth.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Mientras mayor sea la cantidad de agua que ingresa, mayor número de árboles podrás regar y con más velocidad lo harás". As the volume of incoming water grows, you are able to water a greater number of trees and to do so more quickly.
underlying_assumption: A greater flow of water into a plot allows a larger area to be watered in less time.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Passar del rec a manta al rec per goteig generar`a noves plagues.” Switching from flood irrigation to drip irrigation will generate new plagues.
underlying_assumption: Switching from flood irrigation to drip irrigation will generate new pests.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Si vols regar de manera correcta cal que la finca estigui ben arreglada (quan les vores no estan ben fetes gastes més aigua).” If you want to irrigate correctly, the farm must be well arranged (when the borders are not properly made, you use more water).
underlying_assumption: Well-made borders on the field decrease the amount of water that is lost.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Els herbicides eliminen les males herbes i provoquen que l'aigua surti més aviat de la parcel·la.” Herbicides destroy weeds and cause water to exit the plot more quickly.
underlying_assumption: Herbicides encourage the runoff of water over the surface.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Regar bancals de forma alternada separats amb caballons (un sí, un no, un sí, un no) resultava útil en temps de sequera.” Watering beds in an alternating manner separated by ridges (one yes, one no, one yes, one no) was useful in times of drought.
underlying_assumption: Watering beds alternately during a drought aids in saving water and keeping the soil moist.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Quan el bancal queda ben pla, cal regar-lo menys." When the bed is nicely flat, less watering is needed.
underlying_assumption: Levelling the plot to its optimal state reduces the amount of irrigation required.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Quan es fa la plantada arran del canal, cal regar menys.” When planting right beside the canal, less watering is needed.
underlying_assumption: The closeness of crops to water channels lowers how much irrigation they require.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”El agua contenida en las albercas no admite ser guardada por períodos prolongados”. The water held in ponds is not suitable for keeping over long periods.
underlying_assumption: The water from ponds is unable to be kept for an extended period.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Agua que cae del cielo no elimina el riego". Rain falling from the sky does not eliminate the need to irrigate.
underlying_assumption: On its own, rain might not meet what crops require.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Si lo deseo, tengo la posibilidad de llenar la alberca para efectuar el riego en un momento distinto”. Should I wish, I am able to fill the pond in order to irrigate at a different time.
underlying_assumption: The allotted irrigation time may be employed to keep water in a pond for use afterwards.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "La extensión de la parcela influye en la cantidad de agua empleada en el riego". The extent of the plot influences the amount of water applied during irrigation.
underlying_assumption: The demand for water increases in proportion to the size of the cultivated area.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "La manera perfecta de regar consiste en construir los relés y después dar agua allí donde se encuentren los cultivos". The best method for irrigating is to build the distribution channels (reles) first and afterward supply water to the location of the crops.
underlying_assumption: Adequate preparation of the infrastructure guarantees that water is distributed efficiently.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Hay que regar a manta, de lo contrario la tierra se cuartea”. The watering has to be done by flooding; if not, the ground splits open.
underlying_assumption: By keeping cracks from forming due to dryness, flood irrigation preserves the structure of the soil.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Guardamos el agua en la balsa para servirnos de la presión al regar”. We collect water in the pond so as to make use of pressure when irrigating.
underlying_assumption: Storing water at height enhances the efficiency of gravity-driven irrigation.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Acondicionar la acequia antes de los riegos veraniegos contribuye a que se produzcan menos filtraciones”. Getting the ditch ready ahead of summer irrigation contributes to fewer seepages.
underlying_assumption: Upkeep enhances the efficiency of water use.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Hacer cuchillos contribuye a reducir la rapidez del agua y lograr que se mueva despacio filtrándose adecuadamente en la tierra”. Making small earth ridges (cuchillos) contributes to reducing the water's speed, causing it to move slowly and filter properly into the soil.
underlying_assumption: Building small earth ridges reduces the speed of water, thereby boosting infiltration and lessening erosion.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Empleo tasquivas para regar, y antes de que el agua alcance la cola la interrumpo”. I water by means of small distribution channels (tasquivas); I shut off the flow before it arrives at the tail.
underlying_assumption: Managing the flow's distribution enhances both evenness and efficiency.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Cuando riego por calles y preveo que dispondré de poca agua, hago más pequeñas las tasquivas (por donde circula el agua)". When I irrigate by furrows (calles) and anticipate that I will have scarce water, I make the small distribution channels (tasquivas) smaller.
underlying_assumption: Reducing channel size makes the most of a scarce water supply.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Por lo general basta con 3 riegos a lo largo del verano, cada 15 y 30 días como máximo.” In general, 3 irrigations across the summer, spaced 15 to 30 days apart at the most, suffice.
underlying_assumption: Some crops are able to yield even when watered infrequently.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Modificas el cultivo cuando dispones de menos agua (por ejemplo, en lugar de maíz siembras trigo o habas)." You switch the crop when you have less water available (for instance, rather than corn you sow wheat or beans).
underlying_assumption: A lack of water may prompt swapping crops during the sowing period.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Riego por bancales para aprovechar de forma más eficiente la humedad." I water using terraces in order to take better advantage of the moisture.
underlying_assumption: Watering on terraces contributes to retaining moisture in the soil.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Al regar el espárrago se pisa un poco la amelga con el fin de que el agua discurra mejor y no se filtre en exceso.” While watering asparagus, the bed is trodden slightly so that the water runs more and does not soak in too much.
underlying_assumption: A slight compaction of the soil makes water run better and stops it from seeping too much.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”(Cuando conviene sacar mayor provecho del agua) reduzco el ancho de las amelgas.” (When it is necessary to get more out of the water) I reduce the width of the plots.
underlying_assumption: Making the plots less wide allows better use of the water that is available.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "El acondicionamiento del canal de riego influye en que se produzcan más o menos filtraciones." How the irrigation channel is prepared has an impact on whether more or less seepage occurs.
underlying_assumption: Preparing the irrigation channel lessens potential water loss.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Años atrás mojaba un surco de cada dos y dejaba seco el siguiente para no generar exceso de humedad ni favorecer la aparición de hongos, así no echaba tanta agua.” In the past I watered one furrow out of every two and left the following one dry so as not to create excess humidity nor encourage the appearance of fungi, that way I didn't put in so much water.
underlying_assumption: Watering furrows in an alternating pattern assists in managing soil moisture and limiting fungal growth.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”El riego tradicional mediante inundación aporta beneficios al medioambiente, al suelo y a los animales.” Flooding through traditional irrigation brings benefits to the environment, the soil, and the animals.
underlying_assumption: Flooding through traditional irrigation brings benefits to the environment, the soil, and the animals.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Cuando hay sequía, se disminuye la dimensión de la tabla y los caballones se acercan al tallo." When there is drought, the dimension of the plot section is decreased and the ridges are moved nearer to the stem.
underlying_assumption: During a drought, the gap between ridges is narrowed so that less water is consumed.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Aprovechamos de nuevo las aguas ’vivas’ convertidas en aguas ’muertas’, que después vuelven a canalizarse como aguas ’vivas’ una vez más. Nada de agua se desperdicia.” We put ’live’ waters to use again as ’dead’ waters, which are afterward directed back into ’live’ waters once more. Not a bit of water is lost.
underlying_assumption: Within a closed irrigation system, water moves in a cycle where reusing and recirculating it stops any losses from occurring.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Si el agua escasea, abro zanjas para conducir el agua directamente hasta el limonero, evitando inundar.” If water is scarce, I open trenches to lead the water right up to the lemon tree, avoiding flooding.
underlying_assumption: Directing water straight to the lemon tree, rather than flooding, makes water use more efficient in periods of scarcity.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Antaño se detenía el riego antes de que el agua alcanzara el extremo del bancal, ya que el propio impulso del agua la empujaba y aun así conseguía llegar.” In the past, irrigation was stopped before the water reached the edge of the plot, since the water's own momentum pushed it and it managed to arrive anyway.
underlying_assumption: Exploiting the momentum of flowing water allows for saving water while still covering the whole irrigated area.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: ”Cuando la sequía es intensa, permito que el agua fluya por la parcela durante algo más de tiempo.” When the drought is intense, I permit the water to flow across the plot for somewhat more time.
underlying_assumption: Letting water run for a longer period in times of drought enhances the retention of moisture in the soil.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "En épocas de sequía preparo tablas de menor tamaño para aprovechar el agua de forma más eficiente." In times of drought, I prepare smaller plots in order to use the water more efficiently.
underlying_assumption: In periods of drought, reducing the irrigated portion of the plot allows the available water to be used to its fullest.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Si consigo evitar un riego, lo evito." If I manage to avoid an irrigation, I avoid it.
underlying_assumption: Because water and labor have worth, they ought to be employed with care.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "En épocas de sequía construimos caballones para irrigar únicamente la zona de los árboles." During dry periods, we build ridges in order to irrigate the tree area exclusively.
underlying_assumption: The shortage of water demands adaptive irrigation methods that direct water toward the places where it counts the most.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Si cau pluja, no cal que reguis tant." If rain falls, there is no need to irrigate as much.
underlying_assumption: The requirement for irrigation is lessened by rainfall.
main_category: Irrigation practices and communal water management

traditional_knowledge: "Saco partido de la cobertura vegetal que ofrecen las plantas asociadas, las plantas rastreras, tales como la verdolaga (Portulaca oleracea) o el trébol (Trifolium repens)". I make use of the ground cover provided by associated plants, creeping plants, like purslane or clover.
underlying_assumption: Groundcover plants, like purslane and clover, are another way to obtain vegetal cover.

traditional_knowledge: ”En ocasiones empleo una cobertura aérea, instalo un tendido por arriba”. On occasion I employ aerial cover; I install a canopy overhead.
underlying_assumption: Overhead covers made with tarps assist in keeping soil moisture and stop transpiration.

traditional_knowledge: ”El riego varía en función del tipo de cultivo: las hortalizas se riegan mediante caballones, mientras que el maíz, el trigo o la alfalfa se riegan por inundación sobre una superficie amplia”. The way of watering changes according to which crop is grown: vegetables are watered using ridges and furrows, whereas maize, wheat, or alfalfa are watered by flooding across a large expanse.
underlying_assumption: The watering method ought to correspond to the kind of crop being grown.

traditional_knowledge: ”Para regar correctamente, es preciso considerar la inclinación y el desnivel del terreno de la parcela”. To irrigate correctly, one must consider the incline and the slope of the plot's terrain.
underlying_assumption: How the land is shaped influences the movement and spread of water.

traditional_knowledge: ”Para el regadío los suelos arenosos resultan menos adecuados, ya que el agua se cuela más rápido y la capa de la superficie queda seca”. For irrigated agriculture sandy soils are less suitable, since water seeps down faster and the top layer becomes dry.
underlying_assumption: Because sandy soils hold little water, they make irrigation less efficient.

traditional_knowledge: ”Transcurridos tres días desde el riego, remuevo la capa superficial del suelo para cerrar las grietas y conservar una costra que impida que el agua se evapore”. Once three days have passed since irrigating, I stir the topmost layer of soil to close up the cracks and keep a crust that stops the water from evaporating.
underlying_assumption: Working the surface soil following irrigation cuts down on water evaporation by closing the cracks.

traditional_knowledge: "Servirse de la sombra que dan las propias plantas o los demás árboles para conservar la humedad." Using the shade cast by the plants themselves or the other trees to preserve moisture.
underlying_assumption: Making use of the shade cast by plants or trees close by assists in keeping moisture.

traditional_knowledge: "Cuando una parte del terreno cuenta con más grava en el subsuelo, consumirás más agua. Debes arreglar las zonas de mayor permeabilidad." When a part of the terrain has more gravel in the subsoil, you will consume more water. You must fix the zones of greater permeability.
underlying_assumption: When a portion of soil contains more gravel beneath it, water infiltrates more. Zones that are permeable have to be corrected.

traditional_knowledge: "Cuando el agua es escasa, disminuye la extensión de tierra que se riega." When water becomes scarce, the extent of land that is watered decreases.
underlying_assumption: When water is in short supply, the area under irrigation shrinks.

traditional_knowledge: ”El suelo arenoso es el mejor porque conserva mucho mejor la humedad en el fondo.” Sandy soil is the best because it keeps moisture at the bottom much better.
underlying_assumption: Quality soil retains moisture below the surface, even when the top looks dry.

traditional_knowledge: ”Si labras la tierra brota mayor cantidad de hierba y necesitas más tiempo para el riego.” If you till the land, a greater amount of weeds sprouts and you need more time to irrigate.
underlying_assumption: Disturbing the soil through plowing changes how vegetation develops as well as how water behaves.

traditional_knowledge: ”El agua se retiene en una balsa dado que brota en escasa cantidad, con el fin de que gane presión y se incremente el caudal destinado al riego”. Water is held back in a pond since it emerges in small amounts, in order for it to build up pressure and boost the flow used for irrigation.
underlying_assumption: By damming the spring water, one can obtain the proper pressure and flow needed for irrigation.

traditional_knowledge: "Los terrenos de arena resultan pésimos para el riego ya que dejan escapar el agua". Sandy terrain is terrible for irrigation since it lets water escape.
underlying_assumption: Water soaks rapidly through sandy soils.

traditional_knowledge: "La hojarasca, tras arar, la dejo sobre la tierra para que se mezcle y quede más aireada". Once I have tilled, I leave the vegetal remains lying on the earth so they blend in and it turns more loose.
underlying_assumption: Keeping plant residues on the soil's surface once tilling is done helps build up organic matter and enhances the soil's structure and porosity.

traditional_knowledge: ”Dejar la hierba cortada sobre la tierra de la parcela permite conservar la humedad en el suelo.” Leaving the cut weeds on the plot's soil allows soil moisture to be conserved.
underlying_assumption: Leaving mown weeds on the soil preserves its humidity.

traditional_knowledge: ”El plástico colocado encima de los cultivos contribuye a conservar la humedad de la tierra.” Placing plastic on top of crops contributes to preserving the soil's moisture.
underlying_assumption: Covering soil with plastic mulch limits the loss of moisture from it.

traditional_knowledge: ”Los terrenos próximos a los ríos disponen de mayor suministro de agua y resultan más productivos.” The terrains close to rivers possess a greater water supply and turn out to be more productive.
underlying_assumption: Farmlands situated close to rivers receive a greater supply of water and yield more.

traditional_knowledge: ”Si el suelo tiene mucha arena, el agua desciende al subsuelo y se desperdicia.” If the soil contains a lot of sand, the water descends to the subsoil and is wasted.
underlying_assumption: In sandy soils water seeps down to the greatest depth.

traditional_knowledge: ”Con la azada se golpea la tierra para comprobar si aparecen terrones secos.” The soil is struck with a hoe to check whether dry clods appear. A dry clod indicates a lack of humidity.
underlying_assumption: The moisture of the soil may be checked whenever one wishes.

traditional_knowledge: ”Els forats dels talps (bufoneres) obliguen a regar més perqu`e l’aigua s’absorbeix i desapareix.” Because water is absorbed and disappears, mole holes make it necessary to irrigate more.
underlying_assumption: Because water escapes via leakage below the surface, mole holes require additional irrigation.

traditional_knowledge: "Un cop atures de llaurar, ja no podràs tornar a llaurar mai mas perquè les arrels se t'aixequen." Once you cease plowing, you'll never be able to plow again since the roots will come up.
underlying_assumption: Plowing has an impact on the arrangement of roots and on how the soil is managed later on.

traditional_knowledge: ”Observo las precipitaciones de la primavera para averiguar cuánta agua tendré a mi disposición”. I watch the springtime rains to figure out the quantity of water that will be at hand.
underlying_assumption: Spring precipitation levels forecast the quantity of water that will be accessible during summer.

traditional_knowledge: ”Para hacerme una idea de cómo se presentará el verano observo las nevadas tardías de Sierra Nevada; cuando nieva durante marzo o abril, se mantiene agua hasta agosto con un caudal notable”. To form an idea of how the summer will unfold, I observe the late snowfalls in the Sierra Nevada; when it snows during March or April, water lasts until August with a notable flow.
underlying_assumption: The accumulated snow governs how much the rivers flow during summer.

traditional_knowledge: ”Observas la Sierra Nevada para comprobar la cantidad de nieve que tiene (el agua del deshielo abastece el caudal del río)”. You observe the Sierra Nevada to check how much snow it holds (the meltwater supplies the river's flow).
underlying_assumption: The accumulated snow maintains the flow of the river.

traditional_knowledge: ”Si el calor aprieta mucho, procuramos regar durante la noche.” If the heat is very intense, we try to water at nighttime.
underlying_assumption: When the heat is severe, watering at night is preferable.

traditional_knowledge: "Si riegas la papa cuando hace mucho calor se cuece." Watering potatoes during intense heat causes them to cook.
underlying_assumption: Watering certain crops when it is excessively hot damages the plants.

traditional_knowledge: ”Cuando se percibe olor a humedad, viene lluvia.” When a humid smell is perceived, rain is coming.
underlying_assumption: A damp odor in the air is a sign that rain will fall.

traditional_knowledge: ”La sequía provoca que se multipliquen plagas como la araña roja.” Drought makes plagues such as red spider mites multiply.
underlying_assumption: Plagues may be triggered by drought.

traditional_knowledge: ”Nublos colorá: por la tarde traen viento y por la mañana traen lluvia.” Reddish clouds: during the afternoon they bring wind, whereas during the morning they bring rain.
underlying_assumption: The timing and coloration of clouds provide information about weather conditions.

traditional_knowledge: ”(Para averiguar si lloverá) observo la tonalidad del cielo”. (To find out whether it will rain) I observe the tone of the sky.
underlying_assumption: The sky's colour serves as a sign of coming rain.

traditional_knowledge: Saying - "De nieves el año, de bienes el año". Saying - "Of snow the year, of goods the year."
underlying_assumption: Snow that has piled up serves as an indicator that water will be available for irrigation.

traditional_knowledge: "Cuando observas bandas rojizas en el firmamento durante la tarde, significa que se acerca viento". When reddish bands appear in the sky during the afternoon, it means wind is approaching.
underlying_assumption: The presence of reddish streaks in the sky at evening signals that wind is on its way.

traditional_knowledge: ”El momento ideal para trasladar el plantón a la tierra es a finales de invierno y comienzos de primavera, de modo que no le perjudique el frío.” The ideal time to move a sapling into the soil is late winter and early spring, in such a way that the cold does not harm it.
underlying_assumption: The transplanting of saplings ought to take place from late winter to early spring.

traditional_knowledge: "Cel de color roig, vent o pluja." A red-colored sky, wind or rain.
underlying_assumption: When the sunrise or sunset appears red, it indicates coming rain or shifts in the wind.
